overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating on a slate of HDC candidates before the July 8, 2010 meeting, rejected the cure argument, found no Conservation Commission violation, and referred the intentional violation for a fine hearing.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of selectmen gathered before the 7:00 p.m. posted start and discussed board business (HDC and other appointments) outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: That taped discussion, however, demonstrates that the Board members arrived at a collective decision on a slate of candidates.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board also discussed Conservation Commission appointments before the open session on July 8, 2010.
allegations.key_passage: We also did not find evidence that the Board discussed appointments for the Conservation Commission prior to the July 8, 2010 open session, as is alleged in the complaint.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§18-25.
Attendance at an Open Meeting Law training approved by the AG, with certification to the AG that every Board member attended.
Not an order: the violation was found intentional and referred for a hearing under 940 CMR 29.07(3), with a recommended $1,000 fine.
